features.description: `sourcing/album.py` turns one album search's responses and a request's rows into an album-first plan: a primary folder, at most one secondary folder of the same release, per-track rows for the rest, and the ranked remaining folders for a later switch (spec S2-04), pure and without I/O.
steps: Failing tests first in new `tests/test_album_plan.py`, on synthetic responses in the exact shape of `fixtures/search_responses.sample.json` (copy a response dict and change `username`, `files[].filename`, `size`, `bitRate`, `length`, `extension`; never add keys): helper `folder(peer, dirpath, titles, lengths, fmt='flac')` builds one response whose files are `@@music\Al Green\I'm Still in Love With You (1972)\Al Green - I'm Still in Love With You - NN - <title>.flac` for the 9 album titles (the ext-74 shape).

`plan_album(responses, rows, *, policy=DEFAULT_POLICY, listed_lengths=None) -> AlbumPlan` in `sourcing/album.py`: group files by `(username, directory)`; in each folder map rows to files with `scorer.rank([that folder's files], Wanted(row))` (S1-01's title-slot rejection included), each file serving at most one row, highest score first; `primary` = most rows covered (all rows wins outright), then the summed score, then free slot and speed (`Candidate` fields); `secondary` = the folder covering most of the rows the primary lacks, preferring the same release: every shared track's `length` within 2 s of the primary's (or of `listed_lengths` = the S2-03 release's track lengths) and the same format family; a folder covering only one missing row is not a folder source. `AlbumPlan` has `primary: FolderPick | None`, `secondary: FolderPick | None`, `per_track: list[row]`, `alternates: list[FolderPick]` (ranked, excluding primary and secondary), and `assignments(): list[(row, Candidate)]`; `FolderPick` has `username`, `directory`, `rows: list[(row, Candidate)]`, `score`.

The five spec cases pass: (1) one folder with all 9 → primary covers 9, no secondary, no per-track; (2) 7 of 9 in folder A and the other 2 in folder B → primary A (7), secondary B (2), per-track empty; (3) two same-named folders from two peers with all 9 → the higher summed score (bitRate 1000 vs 900) is primary, the other is `alternates[0]`; (4) primary has 7, folder C has the 2 missing but lengths 20 s off (another release), folder D has the same 2 within 2 s → secondary D, C in alternates; (5) nine peers each offering one different track → primary None, secondary None, all 9 rows per_track.

`album.describe(plan, peers=False) -> str` names folders as `folder 1`, `folder 2` (never the `username`), with coverage `7 of 9` and each row → basename; a test asserts no peer name in the text (the fetch header rule).

features.description: Trouble with a planned file switches the rest of that folder's unfiled rows to the next folder of the same release: a transfer error or timeout, a peer that never starts within `ALBUM_START_TIMEOUT_S`, a distrust finding (transcode or wrong recording) or two failures in one folder; the switched folder's queued transfers are cancelled and forgotten, rows already filed stay (spec S2-05, switching).
steps: Failing tests first in `tests/test_album_job.py`, each with two folders in the fake's responses (primary A with 9 files, B with 9 files of the same lengths, another peer): (1) one row's verifier returns an ordinary finding (`duration`) → that row `failed`, the other 8 stay on A, no switch, no `DELETE`; (2) the verifier returns a `transcode` finding for A's first file → the remaining unfiled A rows switch to B: the fake's transfer list has no A record for them (`DELETE …?remove=true` seen, `test_fake_slskd` style), one `POST` to B's peer, every switched row `ok` from B, and a `switch` event `folder 1 distrusted: transcode (<basename>); 8 rows → folder 2`; (3) `FakeSlskdServer(complete=False)` for A's peer only → after `ALBUM_START_TIMEOUT_S` (pass 0.2 s in the test) with no A transfer past `Queued`/`Initializing`, all A rows switch to B; (4) A's first transfer ends `Completed, Errored` (seed the state) → S1-06's `again` switches that row and the rest of A's unfiled rows to B.

`album_job.run` keeps a per-folder failure count; triggers are: `FetchResult` with `again` (S1-06), the start timeout, a verify finding whose kind is in `DISTRUST = {'transcode', 'fake_24bit', 'fake_hires', 'recording'}` (from `verify.HARD_WHEN_STRICT` and `recording`), or 2 failures of any kind in one folder. On a switch: `slskd.remove_download(username, id)` (remove=true) for the folder's records of rows not yet filed, then re-plan the remaining rows with `album.plan_album` over the first search's responses plus one fresh `slskd.search` of the album, with the failed folder excluded (`exclude={(username, directory)}` parameter on `plan_album`) and the same-release preference, then enqueue and continue as S2-05a.
Rows already `ok` or `verify` from the first folder are untouched by a switch (assert their `library_song_id` and status after case 2).
No reason, event or plan text names the peer; the `switch` event names folders by label and files by basename (test asserts).
